own_original_text:
Executive Order 13666 of April 18, 2014 
Expanding Eligibility for the Defense Meritorious Service 
Medal 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Executive Order 12019 of November 3, 1977 (Establishing the Defense Meri-
torious Service Medal), is amended by inserting ‘‘, or to any member of 
the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation,’’ after ‘‘any member of the 
Armed Forces of the United States’’. 
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
April 18, 2014. 
[FR Doc. 2014–09343 
Filed 4–22–14; 8:45 am]

EO 13666 (signed 2014-04-18; 79 FR 22591; held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13666.txt, read in full) is a one-sentence amending order: EO 12019 of Nov. 3, 1977 (Establishing the Defense Meritorious Service Medal) 'is amended by inserting , or to any member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation, after any member of the Armed Forces of the United States'. Inventory: the dossier's single clause covers only the authority recital (chars 719-861), i.e. it omits the operative sentence, so I used one inventory_override (chars 719-1122) covering the recital and the amending sentence. EO 13306 pattern conditions tested for this order: (1) ACT records and dossier missing lines: the dossier has no ACT record and no actor text (actor_provisions empty); EO 12019, the amended order, is held (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12019.txt) and was read in full: its sec. 1 is the sentence the insertion modifies, and EO 12019 contains no sunset; the three standing missing lines (judgment needed for the current predicate; current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256; no attributed legal-text slice for the current-law pointer) are read and ruled out as bases: the basis of this claim is the held original text, not the lead, and the lead is used only as corroboration. (2) Own-term end: none (own_terms is empty). (3) The dossier has no conflicts. (4) The selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning; they cover the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10..14 are not reflected, a stated limit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and the OFR catalog with 17,521 saved order texts (checked 2026-10-19). Corroboration read: the note text for EO 12019 in release point 119-121 (jobs/current-law/output/USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl, note id ida8989a59-3a6f-11f1-a58a-d8db54b14ab5) prints sec. 1 with the inserted words and the status line 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13666, Apr. 18, 2014, 79 F.R. 22591'. This shows the insertion carried into the current compilation of EO 12019 through 2026-10-09; it is held JSONL, not an evidence id, and is used as corroboration only. D6 / later events searched: EDGES.csv has only EO 13666 > EO 12019 (amendment, 2014-04-18) for both orders; a grep of the 6,652 held fr-originals texts (through EO 14435) for 'Executive Order 12019' and for the medal's name finds only EO 12019 and EO 13666; the OFR catalog search (checked 2026-10-19) records no disposition of either; EO 14085 (2022 military-decorations order) was read for 12019 and does not touch it. Limit stated plainly: whether an amending order's 'operative' state is the right model is a rule question for the reviewer; the claim asserts only that the amended text persists in EO 12019 as of the bounded searches.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 13666 has no savings, transition or transfer wording; the insertion is a standing text change in EO 12019, not an accrued right; searches show no instrument that removes, replaces or qualifies it.

current_predicate.legal_basis: EO 13666's one command inserted ', or to any member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation,' into sec. 1 of EO 12019 (Defense Meritorious Service Medal). The insertion took effect on signing (2014-04-18; the order states no other effective date) and remains in the text of EO 12019: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) prints EO 12019 as a note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13666' with the inserted words in sec. 1 and no ending statement. No instrument amending or revoking EO 12019 or EO 13666 is found in the bounded searches.
